Trustworthiness is a critical factor for the widespread adoption of machine learning (ML) systems. This study introduces a novel multi-agent framework that integrates human input to enhance the trustworthiness of black-box ML models. The proposed system employs two specialized agents: a "Human Agent" that facilitates interaction between users and the model to generate human-informed scores reflecting trust levels, and a "Data Agent" responsible for augmenting the dataset using these scores to improve overall model performance. We validate this approach on two distinct datasets, demonstrating that the enhanced agent-driven system effectively boosts both the trust of end-users and the overall data performance of the underlying black-box models.

We introduce a new invariant for knots and links within the torus times an interval, $T^2 \times I$, defined by the trace of an operator constructed via the Hecke modification of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$-quantized Berezin integral applied to the T- and U-matrices of the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ Wess-Zumino-Witten model at large negative levels. This invariant exhibits characteristics consistent with the volume conjecture. We further provide explicit formulas for its values on links formed by the connected sums of torus knots and torus links, as well as for specific families of T- and U-adequate links.

Word Sense Disambiguation (WSD) addresses the challenge of identifying the appropriate meaning of polysemous words within specific contexts. Although numerous methods have been developed to tackle WSD, a significant limitation remains: the scarcity of annotated data for many languages, particularly low-resource ones. To overcome this, we introduce a context-gloss augmentation approach that leverages existing WSD corpora to generate additional sense-labeled training pairs. Our method creates a closed loop where newly produced data is used to train a disambiguation model, which in turn annotates the original corpus to enrich it. We evaluated our approach using a recurrent neural network (RNN) on two languages: English and Indonesian. Results indicate that context-gloss augmentation successfully enhances the performance of these RNN models across both English and Indonesian languages.

This work introduces an integral representation for the inverted $\Gamma$ function involving a regularization term. By leveraging this formulation and its variants, we derive several new integral expressions and establish connections to other structures, including those of the Meijer G-function.

This note reports the first detection of top quark pair production in proton-lead (pPb) collisions. Utilizing data collected at a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 8.16$ TeV with the CMS detector, an analysis of 20 inverse femtobarns ($20\text{ }{\rm fb}^{-1}$) identified 20 candidate events. This count corresponds to a statistical significance exceeding $5\sigma$. The observed cross section, calculated as $\sigma_{\rm obs} = 1.01 \pm 0.12\text{(stat)} \pm 0.07\text{(syst)}$ pb, aligns with leading-order QCD predictions within uncertainties. Furthermore, the measured ratio of top quark pair production in proton-lead versus proton-proton collisions, denoted $R_{\rm dip} = 0.94 \pm 0.11\text{(stat)} \pm 0.07\text{(syst)}$, indicates that initial-state effects in these high-energy interactions are minimal.

This paper introduces a novel end-to-end cross-domain text-to-SQL semantic parsing framework designed to tackle the challenge of limited annotated data when migrating models from one database domain to another. We propose an auxiliary task that guides the end-to-end learning process, aiming to enhance the representation of both natural language queries and SQL statements through the use of pre-trained word embeddings. Our approach leverages a bi-directional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network to encode these embeddings, followed by a multi-grain attention mechanism to capture the semantic structures of the natural language queries. These synthesized representations are then fed into a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) to generate the final SQL output. We evaluated our method on the Spider and Spider-Shopify (SpiderX) datasets, achieving state-of-the-art results with a 93.33% exact match (EM) accuracy on the Spider test set and 89.76% on the SpiderX test set.

We analyze how DP impacts both graph analytics and graph-structured machine learning tasks, while also exploring techniques for integrating private data into these systems. Finally, we outline open challenges in this evolving field.

This study introduces a novel hydrodynamic framework for interacting Bose gases, built upon the Husimi quasi-probability distribution. This approach offers a practical alternative to existing methods, circumventing the mathematical intricacies associated with complex hydrodynamic formulations. The model functions as a closed stochastic partial differential equation, where random noise represents thermal fluctuations. We analyze the system's behavior across varying temperature regimes, demonstrating that the proposed framework accurately reproduces both hydrodynamic and ballistic flow patterns, as well as thermal phase transitions. Furthermore, we investigate the system's approach to equilibrium and the relaxation of non-equilibrium states, specifically focusing on the revival of macroscopic coherence in a one-dimensional interacting Bose gas following a sudden quench from an integrable state.

This paper examines the large deviation behavior of word occurrence frequencies within random, stationary, and ergodic sequences of letters. We establish a general principle applicable to all such sequences and derive specific outcomes for Markovian structures. These findings allow for the characterization of fluctuations in counts for both recurring and rare events.

This note establishes a relative version of a result by Gromov and Schoen, demonstrating that if $\Gamma$ represents the homotopy class of maps from the torus $T^2$ into a proper geodesic metric space $X$ with non-positive curvature, then there exists an embedding $f: S^2 \rightarrow S^2$ such that $f(\partial S^2) = \Gamma$ and $f(S^2)$ is an area-minimizing surface within its relative homotopy class. This conclusion holds specifically when the boundary curve $\Gamma$ is null-homotopic in $X \setminus f(S^2)$, provided $X$ contains no local 2-cuts. Furthermore, we observe that this finding generalizes to any proper geodesic metric space $X$ lacking local 2-cuts, given a simple closed curve $\Gamma$ which is null-homotopic in $X$ and admits a null-homotopy relative to $\Gamma$ avoiding 2-cuts.

The configuration of the ground state and low-lying excited states in $^{64}$Ni has been investigated using gamma-ray spectroscopy. This analysis reveals two shape-coexisting positive-parity structures at energy levels of 2.33 and 253 MeV, identified as [2$^+$$_1$$\otimes$2$^+$$_2$]$_2^+$ and [4$^+$$_1$$\otimes$2$^+$$_2$]$_4^+$, respectively. These findings indicate that a shape-coexisting pair exists at the same spin and parity (J$^\pi$ = 2$^+$), with an energy separation of only 73 keV. The phenomenon is interpreted through the framework of the nucleon monopole-tensor interaction, which generates a strong attractive force between a proton and a neutron possessing anti-aligned orbital angular momentum vectors ($\vec{l}_p$ and $\vec{l}_n$). This interaction facilitates the formation of the low-energy 2$^+$ states by facilitating the occupation of specific intruder orbitals within the $fp$ shell.

We introduce a simple yet effective method for hyperparameter tuning in natural language processing (NLP) that utilizes J-K fold cross-validation. This approach leverages larger batches of data across overlapping validation splits to train models, thereby reducing the variance associated with selecting hyperparameters. We evaluate this strategy on two distinct NLP tasks: machine translation and text classification. The results demonstrate that J-K fold cross-validation effectively improves the consistency of evaluation scores compared to standard K fold cross-validation. Furthermore, we identify that using larger batch sizes is a critical factor in enhancing the method's performance.

Knowledge distillation (KD) is a model compression technique that trains smaller, less expensive models by leveraging the predictions of larger, high-performing models. Among various compression strategies, the knowledge learning (KL) approach stands out for its focus on transferring the capabilities of large models to smaller ones through architectural alignment. This method ensures that the trained student network possesses the same functional structure as the teacher, enabling it to replicate the teacher's operations and achieve comparable performance. This paper reviews the Teacher-Student (TS) architecture family, which includes Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) knowledge learning, Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) knowledge learning, and Vision Transformer (ViT) knowledge learning. We examine how each variant adapts the student to master the teacher's functions and analyze the benefits of ViT knowledge learning over previous methods. Finally, we address current challenges and propose future directions for research in this field.

Graphical models are frequently employed to represent the probabilistic dependencies among variables within a system. A central challenge in working with these models is computing the most probable explanation (MPE), which involves determining the specific configuration of variables that maximizes the joint probability distribution. This task is fundamental for numerous applications, including natural language processing and computer vision. However, existing methods for exact MPE computation are often hindered by the extensive memory required to store and manipulate probability tables. To address this, we introduce a new, succinct representation for functions defined on graphical models that yields a substantial reduction in memory consumption. Empirical results demonstrate that utilizing this concise representation accelerates exact MPE computation and significantly enhances performance in optimisation under constraints.

We report the first measurement of photon recoil effects in single-beam absorption spectroscopy involving an ultracold strontium gas. By analyzing the interaction between a probe laser and atoms near resonance, we observed how the recoil phenomenon alters both the shape and position of the absorption feature. These findings are crucial for enhancing the precision of future optical atomic clocks based on strontium.

Discrete particle suspensions typically exhibit Newtonian behavior, where viscosity remains steady regardless of shear rate. Conversely, at elevated stress levels, they undergo a sudden increase in viscosity—a phenomenon termed shear thickening—that can trigger abrupt transitions to solid-like states. Although industrial applications often aim to prevent such events, understanding their mechanics is equally vital. This work demonstrates that diverse shear-thickening systems, ranging from colloidal particles to granular media, adhere to a unified scaling law for the viscosity tensor. This relationship connects the viscosity matrix to the rate of strain through the dimensionless shear rate, defined by the competition between stress and characteristic particle interaction forces. By integrating this scaling framework with a constitutive model based on the stress tensor, we accurately forecast both the viscosity matrix and the rate of strain. Furthermore, we establish a theoretical basis linking these constitutive properties to the onset of thickening-induced discontinuities.

The Racah algebra $\mathfrak{R}_n$ is defined as the algebra generated by the symmetric polynomials in $n$ variables and the $D_n$ Racah operators, which is known to be isomorphic to the centralizer $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ within the polynomial enveloping algebra of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$. This paper provides an explicit presentation for $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ when $n \geq 3$, demonstrating that it is a quotient of $Z_3(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ generated by the Casimir element and two elements $D$ and $L$ satisfying the $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ relations. Furthermore, we derive the closed-form expression for the Hilbert-Poincar\'e series of $Z_n(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, which factors into the product of Schur $Q$-functions evaluated at $t^2$ and $t$.

Personalization of web search results, though intended to enhance user experience, may cause users to overlook crucial information unavailable in their tailored feeds. This study introduces an experimental framework to assess the extent of relevant data potentially ignored due to Google Web search personalization. The experiment involved 100 participants tasked with identifying the most suitable candidate for a specific job role using a search query related to the position. Participants were divided into two groups: one conducted searches without personalization, while the other did so with it enabled. Results indicated that the group utilizing personalized searches identified the correct candidate significantly less frequently than the group using unpersonalized searches. These findings provide experimental validation that personalization can lead to the omission of significant information, supporting the hypothesis that users may fail to access data they are otherwise capable of locating.

This study investigates the capabilities of a TeV-scale facility where muons collide with protons or ions. We analyze the physics potential, experimental design, and financial requirements for various collision configurations, including proton-proton (pp), proton-antiproton (p-pbar), proton-ion (pA), proton-electron (pe), proton-photon (ppg), proton-neutrino (p-nu), proton-Higgs (p-H), proton-top (p-t), proton-charm (p-c), proton-bottom (p-b), proton-tau (p-tau), proton-D (p-D), proton-B (p-B), proton-J/psi (p-J/psi), and psi(2S) (p-psi2S). We detail the physics potential, experimental setup, and cost structures for each scenario. Our findings indicate that a pp or pA mode offers the most cost-effective path to achieving center-of-mass energies exceeding 15 TeV. Specifically, a pp mode reaching 25 TeV and a pA mode reaching 39 TeV are identified as optimal choices. These high-energy collisions would enable precision measurements of the Higgs boson, discovery of new heavy physics, and precision tests of the Standard Model. Additionally, the pA mode is uniquely capable of producing and studying exotic hadrons, such as the $T_{cc}$ and $Z_c(3900)$ states.

Although respiratory-gated T2-weighted turbo spin-echo (TSE) MRI can mitigate these issues, it typically requires breath-holding, which limits its applicability to patients unable to cooperate with such demands. Conversely, conventional free-breathing TSE sequences offer faster acquisition but suffer from motion blurring due to inconsistent repetition times and lack of gating. This study introduces a novel free-breathing, motion-compensated 4D TSE sequence (4D = 3D plus respiration) designed to address these challenges. Statistical significance testing is a fundamental tool in data analysis, with permutation testing being a prominent example that requires no assumptions about underlying data distributions. However, when computing exact $p$-values for specific, structured test statistics, traditional methods often encounter prohibitive computational costs due to the exponential growth of the permutation space. This paper introduces a novel, efficient algorithm for exact paired-permutation procedures by leveraging the internal structure of the test statistic. Applied to both independent and paired classification tasks, the proposed method achieves a speedup of several orders of magnitude compared to standard approaches.

Additionally, it compiles quarterly statistics on fleet dimensions and aging, alongside yearly data for major port call volumes. To ensure consistency, all monetary values are adjusted for inflation. This unified resource addresses prior limitations caused by discontinuities and incompatibilities in existing datasets, offering a robust foundation for both quantitative modeling and qualitative industry research.

We examine double Higgs boson production at high-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders, utilizing Effective Field Theory (EFT) to investigate the sensitivity of this process to modifications in the Higgs sector. This analysis is particularly relevant for the High-Luminosity Superconducting Hadron Collider (HL-LHC), which will host the Higgs factory. We identify the optimal parameterization for the Higgs couplings to new physics and determine the most promising search channels. Our findings indicate that within the SMEFT framework, double Higgs production offers highly precise probes for BSM physics, with projected sensitivities of $\mathcal{O}(10^{-3})$ for the Higgs trilinear coupling ($\lambda_{3}$) and $\mathcal{O}(10^{-2})$ for the Higgs-gauge coupling ($\kappa_V$). These results remain robust even when considering the interference of other dimension-6 operators.

We examine the Galilean-covariant, metric-affine metric theories of non-relativistic gravity that serve as the c → ∞ limit of General Relativity. Our analysis reveals that the unique Einstein-Hilbert action emerges as the sole solution when the condition of diffeomorphism invariance is upheld. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this result remains valid even if the condition of minimal coupling is substituted with the requirement of spatial rotational invariance.

This study investigates the directional dependence of drag forces acting on cylindrical objects moving through granular beds saturated with fluid. By analyzing the orientation-specific resistance, we identified that maximum drag occurs when the cylinder axis aligns parallel to the flow, whereas perpendicular alignment yields significantly lower resistance. This behavior mirrors drag anisotropy observed in dry granular materials, suggesting that the underlying mechanisms are similar despite the presence of fluid. However, our experiments reveal a distinct departure from dry systems: the yield stress required to initiate motion through the material increases markedly with fluid saturation. Furthermore, we observed a strong correlation between this enhanced yield stress and the specific viscosity of the interstitial fluid. These findings collectively indicate that the mechanisms governing drag anisotropy in fluid-filled beds differ substantially from those in dry systems.

We present a model of $v_n$ generation based on the multiphase transport (AMPT) framework, utilizing its capability to model elliptic flow ($v_2$) in non-central Au+Au collisions as a method to extract the equation of state (EOS) dependent initial spatial anisotropy ($\epsilon$). Applying these findings to central Au+Au and mid-central Cu+Au collisions, we observe that both spatial and momentum anisotropies ($\epsilon$ and $v_2$) increase with the initial transverse momentum ($p_T$). We attribute this trend to the interplay between the equation of state and the geometry of the fireball, which generates a radial pressure gradient that converts initial spatial anisotropy into momentum spatial anisotropy. Furthermore, we note that the extracted EOS-dependent initial spatial anisotropy ($\epsilon$) remains consistent across different $p_T$ ranges. Finally, we find that these results, when combined with measured $v_3$ data, effectively constrain the EOS-dependent initial spatial anisotropy ($\epsilon$) and initial spatial anisotropy ($\epsilon$) in Au+Au collisions.

The ATLAS collaboration at the LHC presents recent findings on sources of $CP$ violation and rare decay processes affecting $B$ mesons. These analyses include direct observations of $CP$-violating effects in neutral $B_s$ mesons, as well as precise measurements of $CP$-conserving rare and suppressed decays of charged $B$ mesons into charmonium states accompanied by light mesons.

We introduce a new approach to accelerate the convergence of full and implicit-CG solvers when applied to discretized systems arising from structure-preserving time-stepping schemes for partial differential equations. Our method involves modifying these matrices via a newly defined class of symmetric, positive definite, and problem-specific (SPSP) preconditioners. We demonstrate the effectiveness of SPSP preconditioners through numerical experiments involving two well-known conservative models: the nonlinear Schrödinger equation and the Euler equations for fluid dynamics.

Scene flow estimation aims to determine three-dimensional motion between consecutive 3D reconstructions of dynamic environments. Although current methods have largely adopted self-supervised learning to achieve high performance, they still depend on manual hyperparameter tuning and architectural choices. While self-supervised metric learning can automate these aspects, existing approaches are hindered by a lack of effective strategies to handle domain shifts across different acquisition systems. In this study, we introduce SceneFlowMetric, a self-supervised metric learning framework that employs adversarial training to ensure robustness against such variations. Our approach utilizes a generator to produce pseudo-3D motion labels and two discriminators: one distinguishes these pseudo-labels from ground truth data, while the other ensures motion consistency. We demonstrate that our method surpasses current state-of-the-art results on the official KITTI benchmark and achieves superior generalization when evaluated on the challenging and distinct Waymo dataset.

We introduce a novel Random Neural Network (RNN) architecture specifically designed for image classification, which integrates analog-valued weights and binary hidden neuron activations. This approach leverages the compact memory footprint and low power consumption inherent to sparse random mappings and binary computations. To further maximize energy efficiency, the proposed RNN features a dynamic data-dependent early-exit mechanism that allows for binary inference with reduced computational load for most inputs. Additionally, the network utilizes a dynamic range allocation strategy for weight storage, optimizing both memory usage and inference speed. Rigorous theoretical analysis and extensive experiments across various benchmarks demonstrate that this model achieves state-of-the-art classification accuracy while maintaining significant reductions in both energy consumption and bit-width complexity.

We investigate the thermodynamic properties and equation of state for spin-polarized quark-gluon plasma under strong magnetic fields and finite temperature, utilizing both perturbative and effective models. Subsequently, we analyze the structural characteristics of spin-polarized strange quark stars in the presence of a strong magnetic field. Our findings indicate that the total mass, radius, and total baryon number of these stars increase with escalating external magnetic field strength. Furthermore, we observe a positive correlation between the star's magnetic moment and the applied field intensity, noting that the magnitude of this moment depends significantly on the specific model employed.

This paper addresses the problem of determining the number of perfect matchings in cubic graphs $G$ that contain a Hamiltonian cycle $C$. We introduce a specific class of graphs denoted as $\mathcal{C}(C)$, defined by the condition that every edge not belonging to $C$ connects two vertices separated by a distance of 2 along the cycle. For any graph within this class, we establish a polynomial-time algorithm to count the matchings. Our findings reveal that for the specific graphs where the algorithm yields a constant count of 9, the non-bipartite 3-cube serves as a unique example. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the algorithm's output equals 9 if and only if the cycle $C$ functions as a valid solution to a specific edge colouring problem associated with $G$.

This paper introduces Timeloops, a novel system-call filtering mechanism designed to enhance the security of containerized microservices. Timeloops operates by learning and enforcing strict policies on which system calls are permissible for specific services, thereby blocking unauthorized interactions with the operating system. A key advantage of this approach is its ability to function without requiring source code access, making it highly adaptable for production environments. To demonstrate the method's efficacy, we deployed Timeloops within a large-scale testbed comprising a production-grade microservices architecture. The results indicate that the proposed policy-learning framework successfully identifies and restricts malicious activities, effectively neutralizing attacks such as container escapes and privilege escalations.

This study introduces a Poisson multi-Bernoulli mixture (PMBM) filter that incorporates a grid-based target birth model, where grid cells containing targets are determined via a softmax function. This approach establishes a spectrum of strategies ranging from purely probabilistic to deterministic target initiation. The method is demonstrated within the framework of sensor management, offering both theoretical and practical applications.

This paper investigates the null controllability within a population dynamics framework subject to interior degeneracy in the diffusion coefficient. We establish a new null observability estimate for the dual problem of the population dynamics, which allows for arbitrary initial population sizes. This estimate is then utilized to demonstrate the existence of null controllability for the system.

Soccer represents a dynamic environment where decision-making is driven by rapid interactions, making it an ideal candidate for applying deep reinforcement learning. This study introduces a novel approach to enhance decision-making in high-stakes soccer scenarios. We developed and trained a deep neural network capable of processing game states and predicting optimal moves. To evaluate the model's efficacy, we created a custom soccer simulation engine and conducted extensive experiments using it. The results demonstrate that the proposed deep reinforcement learning framework significantly outperforms existing baseline methods. These findings confirm the model's potential to improve strategic soccer decisions in critical moments.

Waveform inversion (WI) is a nonlinear technique used in geophysical imaging to reconstruct the velocity structure of the subsurface. Traditionally, WI operates in the frequency domain, processing data independently at each frequency band. Conversely, time-domain WI (tWI) processes data across the entire time window and is recognized for being computationally more efficient. However, tWI often suffers from convergence issues and struggles with resolving complex geological features. This paper introduces a novel time-domain extended WI (tEWI) approach that integrates the benefits of both methods. tEWI combines the computational efficiency of WI with the convergence stability provided by small frequency shifts. By utilizing a narrow time-band, it maintains the efficiency of standard WI while ensuring robust updates. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed tEWI method effectively reconstructs velocity models, successfully recovering intricate geologic structures even in scenarios involving complex wave propagation paths.

We investigate the noisy competitive exclusion principle within a spatial lattice model featuring competition-colonization tradeoffs, where species with superior dispersal abilities displace those with lower dispersal rates. In this framework, established populations can only be displaced by invaders, while colonization rates introduce stochasticity into population dynamics. We demonstrate that this noise disrupts the competitive exclusion principle, allowing for the stochastic coexistence of multiple species. Furthermore, we establish that the noise level directly influences species diversity, with higher noise facilitating greater coexistence. We also examine how the noise parameter affects the average population densities of coexisting species.

This study investigates integrated data and energy networks incorporating Device-to-Device (D2D) communications, with a focus on enhancing D2D performance through Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) assistance. In this framework, an Information Service Provider (ISP) delivers data services to a group of Information Service Users (ISUs) by exchanging signals with D2D links, while simultaneously, an Energy Service Provider (ESP) supplies power to the D2D network via over-the-air wireless charging from the spatially distinct ISUs. The proposed resource allocation strategy jointly optimizes time allocation, transmit power, and charging power to maximize the sum of D2D data rates and harvested energy, subject to constraints on the minimum required data rates and harvested energy thresholds for each ISU. The resulting non-convex optimization problem is addressed via successive convex approximation techniques. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme compared to baseline approaches.

This paper introduces a method for remotely managing a Single-Point Laser Doppler Vibrometer (SP-LDV) to collect two-dimensional data. This approach proves highly effective for applications involving extensive measurement domains where manual repositioning of the SP-LDV is required. The proposed solution integrates an LVDT sensor, a programmable robotic arm, and dedicated control software. This system automatically adjusts the SP-LDV's position and orientation to align the laser spot with target points on an object's surface, which are selected via a user interface. The interface facilitates the input of a 2D coordinate system, allowing operators to define a grid of points and visualize the corresponding trajectories of the laser spot on the respective surface. The paper details the necessary software architecture and presents experimental results that demonstrate the system's functionality and efficacy.

This study introduces a novel concept for utilizing programmable phase plates in Transmission Electron Microscopes (TEM) as dynamic aberration correctors. This profile is mathematically derived from the complex transmission function of the actual correctors, ensuring an accurate approximation. Specifically, experiments showed a 90\% decrease in $C_s$ at 20 nm and 98\% at 40 nm. Furthermore, the method enables real-time, dynamic adjustment of $C_s$ by varying the phase profile, offering a distinct advantage over traditional fixed correctors.

This study investigates the potential production of massive axion-like particles (ALPs) at Belle II via $B$ meson decays, focusing on the scenario where emitted ALPs either remain undetected or manifest as displaced vertices. We derive updated constraints on the effective Lagrangian parameters describing these ALPs interactions.

This study introduces a contextualized approach to identifying and characterizing semantic shifts by leveraging a bidirectional LSTM to generate contextual embeddings for each token. We evaluate this method on two datasets: the historical New York Times corpus, used to examine known changes in the word "crash," and a crowdsourced dataset featuring 1,000 word pairs designed to assess changes in "nice" and "cruel." Our analysis reveals that the contextualized model outperforms both static embedding methods and traditional statistical techniques on these tasks. Additionally, we explore the contextualized embeddings to visualize and examine the nature of these semantic shifts.

The detection of ultralight bosons through the measurement of particle spins in compact objects relies on identifying the characteristic gaps in mass-spin distributions caused by the superradiance mechanism. This approach is applicable to any compact object where a centripetal force—such as gravity or a strong external field—confines a particle near its center of mass while it rotates at a significant fraction of the speed of light. Specifically, we examine the spins of massive quasars, which are typically defined by accretion disks, and demonstrate that the spins of their associated black hole candidates provide sufficient information to determine the mass and spin of ultralight bosons. We analyze two scenarios: first, a standard accretion disk where a particle orbits a black hole under gravitational influence, and second, an exotic compact object where a particle is held by a powerful external field. In both cases, we derive the maximum mass and angular momentum of an ultralight boson as functions of the central object's mass and the boson's own mass. Furthermore, we establish a direct relationship linking the mass of the central object to the mass of the orbiting particle and the spin of the central object to the spin of the particle. Consequently, precise observations of a quasar's location, mass, and spin allow for the derivation of the mass and spin gaps, thereby enabling the detection of ultralight bosons.

Interkinetic nuclear migration (IKNM) involves nuclei moving back and forth along the apical-basal axis during neurogenesis, a mechanism that organizes the developing neural tissue into distinct layers. Although the molecular drivers of this process are well documented, the physical principles governing it remain unclear. To address this, we analyzed IKNM in the embryonic retina of developing *Danio rerio* (zebrafish) using a novel image analysis method that tracks nuclei movement with high temporal and spatial accuracy. We modeled the observed dynamics as a diffusion process, where the diffusion coefficient varies with apical position. Our findings indicate that nuclei move diffusively, with a diffusion coefficient that is highest at the ventricular zone and decreases toward the retinal surface. Furthermore, we propose a new model describing the steady-state nuclear distribution based on this position-dependent diffusion coefficient and a bias in movement direction. This framework successfully accounts for the known molecular cues that direct migration. Collectively, our results suggest that IKNM functions as a diffusive mechanism, potentially facilitating the efficient assembly of the neural layers required for functional vision.

In image reconstruction methods relying on additive separation of color channels, an effective strategy involves designing codebooks that minimize crosstalk among channels during sampling. We address this by formulating and solving a novel optimization problem aimed at minimizing expected squared crosstalk, specifically targeting sampling patterns used in image demosaicing. Although directly computing exact crosstalk is intractable, we introduce a tractable convex relaxation approach to estimate it. Leveraging this estimate, we develop a solution algorithm utilizing alternating minimization to identify an effective codebook. The proposed framework is validated through its application to video recovery from compressed, undersampled data and color restoration from undersampled mosaiced images, demonstrating significant performance improvements when compared to existing codebooks.

We investigate the hydrodynamics of incompressible polar active fluids containing quenched disorder in dimensions $d\geq 3$. By applying a renormalization group analysis to the first order in active density, we determine the leading corrections to the mean flow velocity caused by spatially random forces. Specifically, we examine two configurations of disorder: one where the magnitude of the force fluctuates randomly, and another where the force direction is random but its strength remains constant. For both scenarios, we find that the velocity fluctuation scales linearly with the active density, with a proportionality coefficient that depends on the specific type of disorder. Our results indicate that the velocity fluctuation is more pronounced when disorder arises from directionally random forces compared to those with random magnitudes.

Utilizing Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology, this study aims to extract personal information from Indonesian national ID cards. To evaluate the system's performance, we conducted experiments on a dataset comprising 1,000 images of these cards. The proposed method employs Tesseract for OCR extraction, followed by natural language processing (NLP) techniques to organize and validate the recognized data. Experimental results indicate an F1-score of 0.9999, demonstrating that the system effectively extracts information with high precision and recall.

We employ the Metropolis and heat-bath algorithms within the path integral framework to simulate the quantum harmonic oscillator under various coupling and driving conditions. We verify our simulations by comparing results against exact analytical solutions for both the mean position and its second moment. Finally, we investigate the behavior of the driven quantum harmonic oscillator, analyzing how the mean position and second moment respond to distinct driving protocols.

The rotation acceleration of three asteroids—(10115) 1992 SK, (1685) Toro, and (1620) Geographos—has been modeled by integrating their light curve data with shape information derived from thermal infrared observations and/or high-resolution images. These objects were selected specifically because their spin rates are approaching the theoretical limits for structural integrity. Our results indicate that the predicted rates of spin-up align well with current theories regarding the YORP effect, while also offering valuable insights into the physical properties and potential failure mechanisms of these near-critical asteroids.

The authors demonstrate that the group $\mathrm{Homeo}(S_g)$, consisting of orientation-preserving transformations of a closed surface with genus $g \geq 2$, is not Roelcke precompact when endowed with the compact-open topology. This finding is achieved by disproving an equivalent condition: the absence of a specific type of quasi-conformal cocycle associated with these groups.

Regular mappings from infinite words to infinite words can be equivalently defined using deterministic transducers, rational transduction relations, or compositions of rational relations. In this work, we establish a new characterization based on computable relations and utilize it to demonstrate that regular functions preserving the syntactic type of infinite languages are precisely those whose domain and graph are computable. Furthermore, we examine the inverse problem: given a computable regular function, we present an algorithm to determine whether it is surjective.

Attractors represent the fundamental states of dynamical systems, and their identification is crucial for understanding and forecasting system behavior. However, traditional methods for detecting attractors often struggle with systems exhibiting multiple coexisting attractors, where standard techniques tend to identify only a subset of the possible states. This paper introduces a new methodology based on symbolic dynamics and Lyapunov exponents that effectively discovers attractors without prior knowledge of the system's dynamics. By leveraging a graph neural network (GNN), the proposed approach learns to map symbolic dynamics to specific attractor types, enabling the recognition of multiple coexisting attractors even those never encountered during training. The study demonstrates that this learned symbolic dynamics mapping remains robust against noise and perturbations in symbolic sequences. Furthermore, the method successfully identifies multiple coexisting attractors in both mathematical models and real-world datasets, including the Lorenz system and actual biological data.

This work introduces a second-order computation scheme for elliptic viscosity-solutions of the reachability region within a deterministic nonlinear system, governed by a control input. The proposed method decomposes the associated state-dependent, variational Hamilton-Jacobi-Isaacs (HJI) equation into a sequence of coupled partial differential equations (PDEs), where each order represents an elliptic HJI equation. Specifically, the second-order component is formulated as a state-dependent elliptic HJI problem, while the first-order term functions as a standard boundary condition for the second. By adhering to an iterative framework, the viscosity solution for the state-dependent first-order term is derived initially and subsequently employed to resolve the state-dependent second-order component.

The animacy organization within the human ventral temporal cortex (VTC) has long been debated, with evidence supporting both a categorical arrangement and a continuous gradient of animacy. While the categorical model posits distinct regions for animate and inanimate entities, the gradient model suggests a smooth transition where neural responses correlate with the degree of animacy. Using high-resolution fMRI, we investigated this structure by presenting images of faces, bodies, and scenes alongside objects, animals, and tools. Our findings indicate that the VTC contains a continuous animacy gradient, with face-selective regions peaking at high animacy values and decreasing toward low animacy categories. Furthermore, we observed a spatial segregation between the VTC's animacy gradient and that of object shape, which runs roughly orthogonal to it. These results support the view that the VTC's animacy system is fundamentally continuous, with categorical representations emerging as local maxima along this gradient.

We establish a conditional result demonstrating that, assuming the absence of Landau-Siegel zeros, there exists an effectively computable threshold $N_0$ such that for all weight $k$ exceeding this value, the Hecke-Maust newforms of weight $k$ exhibit the quantum unique ergodicity phenomenon with polynomially effective rates. This achievement relies crucially on the methodology developed by the author in reference [2] regarding the elimination of Landau-Siegel zeros.

Building upon the relational quantum logic introduced by J. B. Hooghuis and colleagues in 2019, we develop a program verification system for relational quantum programs within an expectations framework. This approach allows us to formally establish soundness for key quantum constructs, including monads, the do operator, and the join operation. Our relational formulation offers a distinct advantage over standard, absolute specifications: it captures behavioral relationships between program variants differing only in their monadic components. To demonstrate this benefit, we employ the system to verify the equivalence of two quantum do-notation implementations of the join operator.

Super-spreader incidents, where a single individual transmits the virus to numerous others, are widely recognized as a key driver behind the rapid escalation of outbreaks. This study introduces a mathematical framework to investigate how such events influence the basic reproduction number ($R_0$) and the subsequent epidemic trajectory. Our analysis indicates that super-spreader occurrences invariably elevate $R_0$ and accelerate the onset of the peak infection rate. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these events can precipitate an immediate, sharp rise in infections, effectively causing the peak to occur almost simultaneously. These findings underscore the critical necessity of implementing immediate, stringent containment measures upon detecting a super-spreader to effectively mitigate the outbreak.

Let $X$ denote a complex topological vector space, and $L(X)$ represent the collection of all continuous linear operators acting on $X$. Two operator $T \in L(X)$ is described as codiskcyclic if there exists a vector $x \in X$ such that the closed linear span of $\{p(T)x : p \text{ is a polynomial}\}$ covers the entire space $X$, given $W=\{1, T\}$. This paper investigates the properties of codiskcyclic operators, establishing connections between codiskcyclicity and other cyclicity concepts. Furthermore, it determines codiskcyclicity for specific operator classes, including those with a single eigenvalue, nilpotent operators, and those possessing a finite-dimensional invariant subspace. The study also examines the codiskcyclicity of $T$ in relation to that of its adjoint $T^*$, and provides sufficient conditions for codiskcyclicity when $T$ is a polynomial in some operator $S$ where $S$ itself is codiskcyclic.

Vector magnetic field measurements play a critical role in understanding solar physics, yet gaps exist in direct observations beyond the visible solar disk center. Consequently, these fields are frequently reconstructed using mathematical techniques applied to magnetogram data. Although such inferences offer valuable insights, they can inadvertently introduce biases that skew statistical analyses. This study examines the origins and effects of these biases within key magnetic field statistics, specifically the magnitude and polarity asymmetry. We demonstrate that non-uniform sampling rates and the geometric limitations of disk-edge extrapolations both contribute significantly to these asymmetries. To address this, we propose a new methodology designed to detect and reduce bias in these inferred metrics. Furthermore, we apply a statistical framework to evaluate the statistical significance of any residual asymmetries after correcting for identified biases.

Deforming the integration contour offers a method to alleviate the sign problem within Monte Carlo simulations of out-of-equilibrium quantum systems, yet it frequently induces a severe fitting sign problem when utilizing neural networks to represent important distribution ratios. We introduce a complex-valued architecture that overcomes this obstacle, demonstrating a tenfold reduction in statistical error compared to current state-of-the-art methods in various many-body scenarios.

This paper investigates the preservation of topological entropy and factor complexity under monoid morphisms, specifically analyzing their behavior when these invariants are expressed in terms of the length function associated with the morphism. Additionally, we examine how a change of basis in a free group influences these quantities, deriving explicit formulas for their transformation. Finally, we apply this framework to address a question originally posed by Blanchard and Hansel regarding complexity and entropy within symbolic dynamics.

We introduce a Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) framework designed to facilitate cross-task generalization in natural language processing (NLP) without requiring unsupervised labels. This approach enables a model trained on Task A to be adapted for Task B by leveraging RAG to retrieve relevant data from Task B and incorporate it into the training of the Task A model. The retrieved information allows the Task A model to learn Task B's characteristics while retaining its existing proficiency in Task A. We evaluated this method on two distinct natural language inference (NLI) tasks: the MultiNLI dataset and the XNLI dataset. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach successfully enhances Task B performance using only a few labeled instances from Task B, while maintaining Task A performance levels comparable to those achieved when training exclusively on Task A data.

We introduce a strategy to optimize hyperparameters for differentially private stochastic gradient descent (DPSGD). This approach combines a broad spectrum of privacy-preserving techniques with a specific method for estimating the sensitivity of updates within DPSGD. We validate the effectiveness of this framework across three distinct domains: image classification, generative adversarial networks (GANs), and reinforcement learning.

This work introduces the novel structures known as Boolean complexes of involutions (BICs) and investigates their properties. We establish that the BICs of n+1 distinct involutions form a subcomplex within the n-skeleton of the infinite symmetric group's Cayley graph. Furthermore, we determine the precise dimensions of these complexes for various classes of involutions. The paper also explores connections between BICs and other combinatorial objects, including signed permutations, set partitions, and the specific counts of involutions characterized by their cycle structures. Finally, we present several new, explicit formulas for the BICs of n+1 distinct involutions.

We introduce a novel methodology for mapping the chemical evolution of the Milky Way disk, designed to handle the intricate abundance patterns revealed by the APOGEE survey. Our approach employs a two-component model that fits the data using both absolute and residual abundances, allowing for the identification of stochastic processes through deviations in residuals while capturing systematic trends via absolute values. Applied to the Mg, Fe, and $\alpha$ element suites from the GJ-155 sample of APOGEE, our results indicate that a model incorporating both stochasticity and chemical enrichment is superior to those relying on enrichment alone. Furthermore, we demonstrate that a model based solely on residuals underperforms compared to our hybrid method. Finally, we establish that this new framework provides a more robust tool for charting the Galaxy's chemical history.

This study examines the transmission patterns of Chinese online rumors regarding the COVID-19 pandemic, aiming to assess their impact and underlying drivers. The authors investigate the geographic origins and propagation pathways of these rumors, analyzing the correlation between their dissemination and the real-world movement of individuals. Furthermore, the research evaluates the rumor-related harm across multiple dimensions, including public health, government credibility, and social stability. The work offers a novel methodology for quantifying rumor influence and introduces a new index designed to measure the severity of such rumors. Finally, the authors explore the key factors contributing to their viral spread.

We present a planetary nebula (PN) catalogue for the galaxies within the Fornax Cluster, assembled from deep, wide-field images obtained with the 2.3-m Isaac Newton Telescope (INT) at the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory. This dataset includes new distance estimates derived from surface brightness fluctuations (SBF) of red giant branch stars, calculated independently for each galaxy using PNs as surface brightness photometric standards. These SBF measurements were conducted for six galaxies—NGC 1399, NGC 1404, NGC 1360, NGC 1316, NGC 1399, and NGC 1404—across three distinct regions of the cluster: the core, the northeast arm, and the northwest arm. The resulting SBF distances for these six galaxies are compared against a sample of 13 galaxies with previously published PNs-based SBF distances (Hernquist & Ford 1992). LifeStream is a streaming processing engine designed to handle periodic data streams, addressing the performance limitations found in current systems when managing concurrent streams. While existing solutions typically optimize for high throughput of random data, they often incur significant overhead when processing periodic streams, which follow predictable patterns. LifeStream leverages these patterns to deliver superior performance, achieving up to a 100-fold increase in efficiency compared to traditional engines.

Loss functions serve as a critical hyperparameter in deep learning, yet their optimal selection often relies on intuition or empirical testing. This study introduces a systematic approach to evaluate how different loss functions influence deep neural network performance across various classification tasks. By analyzing these choices through the lens of generalization error decomposition, the research offers new insights into the consequences of loss function changes and establishes clear guidelines for their effective utilization.

This study introduces a novel thermomechanical model designed to simulate the structure evolution of amorphous polymers undergoing strain-induced crystallization (SIC). The framework integrates the Giesekus constitutive equation for amorphous polymers with a kinetic model based on the evolution of crystallinity. This kinetic approach relies on the concept of orientation-dependent nucleation rates, which are determined by the degree of chain alignment within the amorphous matrix. The model's validity is assessed by comparing its predictions against experimental data on the mechanical behavior and microstructural changes of polybutadiene (PB) and polystyrene-block-polybutadiene-block-polystyrene (PS-b-PB-b-PS) copolymers. The results indicate that the proposed model effectively captures both the mechanical response and the development of SIC-related microstructures in these amorphous polymers.

This study examines how a doped nematic $d$-wave superconductor responds to an external magnetic field. We find that, unlike conventional superconductors, this system exhibits a positive magnetic susceptibility. This behavior stems from the formation of momentum-space bound states between electron pairs with opposite momenta but identical nematic orientations. These "Cooper pairs of triplet states" possess a finite magnetic moment, and their paramagnetism is driven by the exchange interaction between pairs of the same momentum. We further demonstrate that this induced paramagnetism can be suppressed by lowering the symmetry of the disorder potential.

Conventional non-coherent differential detection for continuous phase modulation (CPM) with a minimum symbol delay of $m=1$ offers a robust balance of low implementation cost and resilience to carrier frequency offsets, yet it suffers from suboptimal bit-error rate (BER) performance due to signal space compression. This study presents an enhanced differential detection framework for CPM that employs conventional trellis-based decision-making but utilizes an optimized transition delay, $\tau_{opt}$, rather than the standard one-symbol interval. We derive a closed-form expression for this optimal delay applicable to arbitrary modulation indices and demonstrate numerically that implementing $\tau_{opt}$ yields significant performance gains across various schemes. Specifically, a differential 2/4-DPSK system achieves a 1.5 dB improvement at a constant BER, while a differential 2/4-DSK sees a 2 dB gain; for the 2/4-DPSK case, $\tau_{opt}$ equals approximately 0.57 symbols.

We investigate the quantum capacity of a thermal Minkowski vacuum, evaluating it through the measurement of vacuum compressibility. By deriving an exact formula for this compressibility in terms of temperature, we assess how thermalization influences both the capacity to transmit quantum information and the mechanical response of the vacuum. Our analysis reveals that vacuum compressibility reaches its maximum at criticality ($T_c = 0$) and diminishes monotonically as temperature increases. Furthermore, we explore the impact of external influences—specifically an accelerating observer and a gravitational field—on these properties.

Although the quantum linear system solver offers a theoretical exponential speedup, its practical application for solving $Ax=b$ on current hardware is hindered by a reliance on precise arithmetic. This requirement is unfeasible for current noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices, which operate with limited bit depth. This work introduces a hybrid algorithm tailored for NISQ hardware that approximates the solver's amplitude estimation using a discrete Fourier transform (DFT). By trading a modest increase in polynomial runtime for compatibility with existing devices, the proposed method achieves a quadratic speedup relative to standard Harestam's algorithm. Furthermore, we present an optimized DFT implementation that reduces the DFT order, thereby decreasing circuit complexity and enhancing success probability. Finally, we validate the algorithm's efficacy through simulation, demonstrating its ability to execute two distinct amplitude estimation-based portfolio optimization strategies for realistic, large-scale instances.

This paper introduces a Multi-Modal Neural Network (MMNN) that integrates bidirectional attention mechanisms to enhance speech recognition. The proposed model trains on both audio and text data, utilizing the text to establish a robust bidirectional connection between the current utterance and its corresponding acoustic segments. This approach aims to leverage the inherent semantic structure of text to improve the precision of speech understanding. The model was evaluated on the Switchboard corpus, with results indicating a notable 10.3% reduction in Word Error Rate (WER) compared to a baseline system trained solely on audio.

Consider $n$ cars navigating an avenue with $n$ parking spots, where each driver has a preferred location $a_i$ chosen uniformly from the range $\{1, \dots, n\}$. A vehicle can occupy a spot only if it matches its preference or if those positions are already occupied; upon arrival, it takes the nearest available slot at or beyond its preference. An $n$-tuple of preferences qualifies as a parking function if every driver successfully parks. This study investigates the asymptotic behavior of the initial $k$ preferences within such tuples. Specifically, we derive limit laws for the initial $k$ values when $k$ remains fixed while $n$ approaches infinity, and we examine the scenario where $k$ scales proportionally to $n$.

We report on the electrical transport characteristics of individual NbN nanowires, where a voltage gate modulates conductance through quantum phase-slips. Our findings indicate that conductance modulation occurs even in the absence of a Josephson junction, suggesting that coherent quantum phase-slips, rather than Coulomb blockade, are the primary mechanism behind gate-controlled conductance in these NbN nanowires.

Video prediction involves anticipating future object movements within a scene based on current and past visual data. We introduce a novel approach utilizing a dual representation of historical and present views to forecast objects from unseen camera angles. This method employs a hierarchical architecture where the top level identifies object motion patterns, and the bottom level simulates these motions using convolutional recurrent networks to generate video frames. Our experiments demonstrate that this model effectively predicts object behavior in both dynamic and static environments, achieving superior accuracy in handling complex, real-world scenarios compared to existing techniques.

Inter-orbital coupling describes the influence that electrons occupying one orbital have on those in a different orbital. This phenomenon is typically characterized by a weak interaction strength, which often results in subtle effects that are difficult to detect. Nevertheless, such coupling can drive significant structural and functional changes in materials, including the emergence of exotic magnetic states, the formation of unconventional superconducting pairs, and the creation of Mott insulators. In this study, we report the experimental detection of strong inter-orbital coupling within a two-dimensional triangular lattice of ultracold atoms. By utilizing two distinct atomic orbitals, we engineered a tunable, repulsive interaction between them. Our measurements reveal that this coupling strength is an order of magnitude greater than previously observed in other systems.

The $\Omega^{-}$, composed of three strange quarks ($sss$), represents the heaviest and most significant baryon containing only strange quarks. This study employs the relativistic four-component chromodynamic quark model to investigate the $\Omega^{-}$'s spectrum, magnetic moments, and transition moments. Our findings reveal a $1/2^{-}$ negative-parity excited state at 1717 MeV, suggesting this state serves as the ideal candidate for the long-identified $1/2^{-}$ resonance at 1695 MeV. Additionally, we report a predicted mass of 1856 MeV for the $3/2^{+}$ state, which corresponds to the experimentally observed $3/2^{+}$ baryon at 1880 MeV. We also calculate the magnetic moments and transition moments for all spin states of the $\Omega^{-}$, providing these results to aid future experimental investigations.

Airborne disease transmission on urban transit, such as buses, is influenced by ventilation, exhalation rates, and the inhalation efficiency of both passengers and drivers. This study employs a well-mixed model to forecast transmission among these groups, utilizing a two-compartment framework that distinguishes between individuals and the vehicle interior. We investigate how transmission probabilities vary with ventilation rates, the number of occupants, and the exposure duration. Our findings indicate that transmission risk escalates with higher passenger counts, longer exposure times, and poor ventilation, while remaining largely unaffected by exhalation rates or inhalation efficiency. Furthermore, the model predicts that transmission risk increases non-linearly with passenger volume, suggesting that the well-mixed approach may overestimate infection likelihood in crowded conditions. Overall, despite inherent simplifications, the well-mixed model effectively captures the primary drivers of disease spread on urban buses.

The Spin-Orbit Proximity Effect (SOPE) describes the transfer of strong spin-orbit coupling from heavy metals to adjacent materials with lighter atoms, significantly influencing their magnetic properties. This study investigates the impact of interface scattering on the SOPE within Bi/Co multilayers, where cobalt's magnetization aligns perpendicular to the interface. Utilizing the non-equilibrium Green's function method, we calculate the magnetization and spin-orbit torques (SOTs) generated by the Bi-induced spin Hall effect. Our results indicate that interface scattering markedly diminishes the Bi-driven SOTs and the associated spin accumulation. Consequently, this scattering reduces the induced SOT efficiency and compromises the ability of spin accumulation to modify the anisotropic magnetization reversal field.

This paper investigates the time-independent fractional Schrödinger equation in $N$-dimensional space for a generalized Mie-type $N$-dimensional potential under Jumarie's fractional derivative framework. By applying the Nikiforov-Uvarov method, the paper derives the equation's radial fractional counterpart. We demonstrate that this radial fractional equation admits an exact solution, allowing for the construction of the wave function and the associated generalized Mie-type potential. Specifically, we analyze two cases: first, we consider a potential where the Mie parameter $\lambda$ remains constant, deriving the explicit form of the potential and the corresponding fractional radial equation; subsequently, we examine the scenario where $\lambda$ varies with the radial coordinate $s$. Finally, we analyze the physical properties of the generalized potential and its corresponding fractional radial equation.

This study examines the enforcement of explicit Lipschitz continuity constraints on neural network functions, a practice that remains under-explored despite the significance of such bounds. We introduce an iterative optimization framework designed to optimize a target objective while simultaneously adhering to these Lipschitz requirements. Our analysis reveals that this approach functions as a regularizer, enhancing generalization performance. Additionally, we establish a connection between these Lipschitz constraints and standard weight decay techniques. Empirical results from classification benchmarks on ImageNet and object detection tasks using MS COCO support our findings, demonstrating improved generalization with constrained networks compared to their unconstrained counterparts.

This study examines NLO QCD corrections to Drell-Yan lepton-pair production within third-generation gauge vector leptoquark (LQ) models, a class of theories motivated by recent anomalies observed at B-meson factories and the LHC. The calculation employs the POWHEG-BOX framework to integrate these NLO QCD results with parton showering, enabling direct comparison with LHC data on $t\bar{t}$ and $W$+jets processes. By analyzing these datasets, we derive updated constraints on the parameter space of vector LQ models. Furthermore, we project how potential future enhancements in the precision of dijet and $W$+jets measurements at the High-Luminosity LHC could further restrict these theories.

Centering Theory (Grosz et al., 1995; Regier and Goldberg, 1993) offers a robust framework for analyzing the coreferential patterns of human language. This study examines whether integrating this theory can enhance neural coreference resolution models. We introduce a new dataset of coreferential structures for news text and train a neural algorithm to predict Centering Theory attributes. Furthermore, we develop a context embedding that incorporates these predicted attributes and employ it within a neural coreference classifier. Experimental results indicate that this context embedding outperforms existing methods, and utilizing Centering Theory features yields a statistically significant improvement in coreference performance.

WiFi fingerprinting is a well-established method for indoor localization, yet its broad adoption has been hindered by the high costs and logistical complexities associated with manual data collection. This study introduces a machine learning framework designed to estimate distance from access points using only raw, uncurated WiFi signal strength data. We evaluated the approach in a large, multi-purpose university building, testing various algorithms and signal processing techniques. The results indicate that a simple linear regression model, applied to the minimum received signal strength values without extensive preprocessing, achieved the highest accuracy with a root mean square error (RMSE) of 1.73 meters. This performance surpasses that of more sophisticated nonlinear models, suggesting that the most significant source of inaccuracy stems from the lack of precise ground-truth distance measurements in the training set rather than the choice of algorithm. Consequently, the paper argues that leveraging inexpensive, real-world WiFi datasets is feasible for WiFi-based ranging applications.

Beam breakup instability (BBU) represents a primary constraint on the achievable beam current in high-field superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavities. In energy recovery linacs (ERLs), BBU susceptibility is significantly influenced by bunch structure, specifically the distribution of longitudinal charge and the pattern of transverse emittance. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of how filling patterns impact BBU thresholds, utilizing a new, rigorous derivation of the BBU transfer function that explicitly incorporates both longitudinal charge and transverse emittance distributions. The transfer function is evaluated for various patterns, including those generated by the Fermilab ERL, the Jefferson Lab ERL, and the proposed Spallation Neutron Source at the European Spallation Source. Results indicate that BBU thresholds can vary by up to a factor of 10 depending on the specific filling pattern. These findings are critical for the design and optimization of future high-current ERLs.

We derive the one-loop central-emission vertex for a gluon radiated centrally in $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, involving quarks and gluons at the parent line. This six-point vertex is constructed via BCFW recursion and differential equations, with boundary conditions set using color-ordered vertices. The resulting central vertex is confirmed to be the square of a six-point one-loop MHV amplitude divided by the total charge of the radiated gluon. We further establish a connection between this vertex and the previously identified one-loop central three-point vertex.

This study investigates the structural characteristics of strongly stretched polymer brushes, focusing on how their geometry influences the formation of end exclusion zones (EZs). An analytical model is developed for molten brushes of arbitrary shape, predicting that the width of the EZ scales as $N^{-1/2}$, where $N$ denotes the degree of polymerization. This finding indicates that end segregation occurs in molten brushes regardless of their configuration. The findings are substantiated by molecular dynamics simulations across various geometries, which also reveal a distinct "end accumulation zone" situated at the brush periphery, opposite the EZ. Furthermore, the research examines the impact of monomer-monomer and monomer-solvent interactions on both the EZ and end accumulation zone, alongside the effects of polydispersity.

We propose a machine learning approach to analyze all-sky data from the Fermi-LAT telescope, aiming to enhance the sensitivity map by refining photon counts within specific energy bands. Utilizing a year of data, we apply a Poisson-gamma likelihood function to determine the mean photon count for each 2-degree-field-of-view (2-FOV) region, estimating these values alongside their uncertainties. Our findings indicate that the proposed method outperforms traditional counting statistics, achieving approximately a 10% reduction in variance for low-sensitivity areas. We present the resulting enhanced all-sky map, which offers improved clarity in identifying and highlighting variable astrophysical sources.

We examine the challenge of maximizing a differentiable, symmetric $k$-player game where the payoff function depends on the actions of all participants and the specific ordering of moves. In this context, a "dictatorship" restricts players to act strictly sequentially. We demonstrate that any local optimum within a dictatorship yields a gradient with a significantly smaller norm than the smallest possible gradient found in the unrestricted, full game space. These enhanced bounds are applied to analyze Dictatorship Cournot competition, revealing that restricting players to act sequentially reduces the gap between the social welfare at the Nash Equilibrium and the first-best outcome by a factor of up to $\sqrt{n}$ compared to the standard, unstructured game.

This study utilizes a custom algorithm to analyze approximately 1.5 petabytes of 3-gigapixel archival data from the Pan-STARRS1 3p instrument, aiming to identify binary asteroid systems. The method involves a multi-stage process: initial detection of asteroid tracks, extraction of individual asteroid crops, and detection of secondary bodies within those images. This approach successfully identified 1,000 candidate binary systems with primary bodies larger than 1 km, corresponding to a detection efficiency of roughly 50% for such systems. Statistical analysis of the derived separations and brightness ratios indicates that the observed distributions of these properties are consistent with those of previously studied samples. Furthermore, the algorithm's performance was validated against known binary systems from the Virtual Asteroid Observatory database, demonstrating a recovery rate of 98% for primary objects exceeding 10 km in diameter within the dataset.

This paper presents auxiliary assumptions and estimation techniques for network econometrics, specifically focusing on the identification of semiparametric partial linear models under network-generated data. Such models are highly relevant in network analysis, where certain regressors are estimated via linear methods while others are determined nonparametrically. We establish sufficient conditions for consistency and asymptotic normality, accommodating both sparse and dense network structures. These theoretical developments enable the examination of network peer effects within broader semiparametric frameworks. The research concludes with an empirical application assessing the impact of high school attendance on individual outcomes.

This paper establishes several forms of addition and differentiation rules specifically for Riemann-Liouville variable-order fractional integration and differentiation. It introduces an innovative representation of the Riemann-Liouville variable-order fractional integral as a convolution between a constant function $\gamma$ and a Fox H-function. Utilizing this representation, the author derives addition and differentiation formulas for both the Riemann-Liouville and Caputo variable-order fractional integral and differentiation operators. These results are further applied to H-type functions and Riemann functions to develop addition and differentiation formulas for these specific function classes.

We introduce MindTheDice, a framework designed to teach theory-of-mind (ToM) and intent recognition in human-computer dialogue. Unlike existing methods that rely on explicit ToM annotations, MindTheDice infers these capabilities through natural interaction. Our system employs a hybrid intent model combining task-oriented and open-domain approaches to detect user goals, infer mental states, and execute appropriate actions. We validate our approach in a Dungeons and Dragons campaign where the AI assumes the role of a player. Experiments demonstrate that incorporating ToM significantly boosts user engagement and the effectiveness of the AI's guidance compared to baseline systems.

Proteins are knotted through self-assembly, yet the mechanisms driving this process and the resulting topological constraints on their function remain unclear. This study introduces a methodology to identify knotted folding trajectories by analyzing the relationship between a polypeptide chain's native state and its surrounding topological environment. The approach involves generating a vast ensemble of structures containing the specific knotted motif found in the native state, selecting those with minimal root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) from the native conformation, and utilizing the resulting subset as a representation of the folding pathway. Applying this technique to three knotted proteins—Tye7, JujB, and Uch35—reveals that the formation of the knot occurs early in the folding process, with the knot becoming topologically trapped by native-like secondary elements prior to the full establishment of the tertiary structure.

This work establishes that the group of symplectic diffeomorphisms, denoted $\text{Diff}_\omega((T^2,k)\# \overline{\mathbb{C}P^2})$ acting on $( (T^2,k)\# \overline{\mathbb{C}P^2},\omega )$, maps to simple cohomology classes. Here, $T^2$ represents a torus with a positive integer $k$, and the symplectic form $\omega$ satisfies the non-degeneracy and taming conditions. Furthermore, this group generates the corresponding symplectic mapping class group.

The Anomalous Nambu-Goldstone Theorem addresses a scenario in which relativistic or nonrelativistic quantum field theory exhibits an accidental continuous global symmetry that is anomalous, thereby preventing the theory from being consistently defined on its own. We establish the theorem within both relativistic and nonrelativistic quantum field theory frameworks. We further demonstrate that the theorem holds true for the Kondo effect within the realm of relativistic or nonrelativistic quantum field theory.

We introduce D3-LLaMA, a data-driven approach designed to enhance the factual robustness of the open-source T5 model. Although NLP systems have advanced significantly, they remain vulnerable to paraphrasing errors, where semantically altered sentences cause a model to flip its original predictions. To address this, we utilize a powerful, instruction-tuned 70B-parameter language model to generate counterfactual outputs for D3-LLaMA training data. This process involves taking an input and its associated label, using the large model to create a variation that preserves the classification but alters the outcome, which is then used to update the T5 base. The resulting model demonstrates a 3.3% improvement in F1 scores on the SciQ dataset compared to the untrained version.

Thin films of off-stoichiometric Heusler alloys typically exhibit poor crystalline quality when deposited on conventional substrates. This study demonstrates that depositing full Heusler compounds on a graphene layer atop sapphire enables high-quality growth via van der Waals epitaxy. Specifically, Fe2NiSi films formed on this interface display a narrow full-width at half-maximum of 0.12° in rocking curves and exhibit a 100-fold reduction in twin defects compared to those grown directly on sapphire. Although direct growth on graphene favors a (001) orientation with high crystallinity, it initially produces polycrystalline material containing numerous twins. By adjusting deposition parameters, we successfully induced remote epitaxy, yielding single-crystalline Fe2NiSi. Remarkably, these engineered defects function as recombination centers that enhance the minority carrier lifetime of the resulting semiconductors.
